name: Sosthenes (synagogue ruler)
title: The synagogue ruler in Corinth
summary: Sosthenes was the synagogue ruler in Corinth during Paul's stay there. He was beaten by the crowd before the proconsul Gallio's court after the Jews' charges against Paul were dismissed. He may be the same Sosthenes later mentioned as a co-sender of Paul's first letter to the Corinthians, which could indicate that he became a Christian.

keyEvents.title: Becomes synagogue ruler
keyEvents.description: Sosthenes likely took over as synagogue ruler in Corinth after Crispus, the former ruler, became a Christian and left the synagogue.

keyEvents.title: The Jews' charges against Paul are dismissed
keyEvents.description: The Jews in Corinth brought Paul before proconsul Gallio and accused him of persuading people to worship God contrary to the law, but Gallio rejected the case as an internal religious matter.

keyEvents.title: Is beaten by the crowd
keyEvents.description: After Gallio dismissed the charges against Paul, the crowd seized Sosthenes and beat him in front of the court. Gallio did not care about this.

keyEvents.title: Possible co-worker with Paul
keyEvents.description: A Sosthenes is mentioned together with Paul as a co-sender of the first letter to the Corinthians. If this is the same person, it suggests that he later became a Christian and a fellow worker with the apostle.
